question: When did first contact happen?
what the sources say: S14 marker: 7:30 a.m. | S02 Gamble: "About 8 o'clock" the enemy was reported approaching the pickets | S01 Buford: reports came in "between 8 and 9 a.m."
how the pilot handled it: Used 07:30 for the first shot (P02, P14) and 08:00 for the brigades forming (P04, P06).
comment: The reports record when word reached each headquarters, which is later than the first shot. Watches were not synchronized.
v2 update: what the map adds: No map evidence on the first shot.
v9 check: Reardon and Vossler (S55): The booklet has troopers of the 8th Illinois Cavalry sight the column about 0700 and Lt. Marcellus Jones fire the first shot then (p. 19), half an hour before the marker's 7:30. It also dates the first phase of the day from 0700 (p. 20). The playback still uses 7:30; you agreed that time before this source was read.

question: Where did Archer first meet the pickets?
what the sources say: S07 Hill: "About 3 miles from Gettysburg" | S06 Shepard: after advancing "about 3 miles" from camp near Cashtown, then the pickets fell back "about 3 miles" | S01 Buford: enemy pickets on 30 June were "about 4½ miles from Gettysburg" | S11 tablet: marched about six miles
how the pilot handled it: Used the First Shot marker site, 3 miles from Gettysburg (P02, P14).
comment: Shepard may describe an earlier contact with vedettes farther west. Cashtown is about 8 miles out, so 3 miles from camp is about 5 miles from Gettysburg.
v2 update: what the map adds: No new evidence. The First Shot marker lands about 70 m from the pike junction as the map draws it, which is within the map's error at its west edge.

question: When did Heth deploy and advance?
what the sources say: S04 Heth: mentions "9 o'clock" as the time he was still ignorant of the force ahead | S05 Davis: line of battle formed "About 10.30 o'clock" | S11, S12 tablets: both brigades crossed Willoughby Run about 10 a.m. | S16 (modern): deploy 9:00, advance 9:30
how the pilot handled it: Used 09:30 for the lines on Herr Ridge and 10:00 for crossing the run (P17, P18, P20, P24).
comment: Davis's 10:30 cannot be squared with the tablets' 10 a.m. crossing. A reviewer should rule.
v2 update: what the map adds: New evidence. The map labels Archer's line, Davis's line and Gamble's line all "9 A.M.", and Davis east of the run "10.15 A.M." (P37). You agreed with 09:30, so v2 leaves the times alone. If you prefer the map: set P17, P20 to P23 and P32 to P36 to 09:00 and end the P16 halt at 09:00.
v3 update: Held in the data as a start range, 9:00 to 9:30, on P16, P17, P20 to P23 and P32 to P36.
v9 check: Reardon and Vossler (S55): The booklet has Archer's brigade halt on Herr's Ridge about 1000 to wait for the rest of the division, and Reynolds's leading division arrive at roughly 1015 with the attack over Willoughby Run in between (pp. 19-20). That is an hour later than Bachelder's "9 A.M." label for the Herr Ridge lines and leaves 15 minutes for the attack. The data still holds 9:00 to 9:30 for Herr Ridge and 10:00 for the run. A ruling is needed again.

question: How far out was Heth when he deployed?
what the sources say: S04 Heth: "within a mile of Gettysburg" | S05 Davis: artillery opened "within about 2 miles from town" | S12: line formed west of Herr's Tavern
how the pilot handled it: Placed the lines on Herr Ridge (P17, P20).
comment: Herr Ridge is roughly 2 miles from the town centre by the pike; Heth's "mile" looks loose.
v2 update: what the map adds: Measured on the map: Herr Tavern is 2.97 km (1.85 miles) from the town square and Archer's line about 1.74 miles. That fits Davis's "about 2 miles"; Heth's "within a mile" does not fit. New disagreement: tablet S12 says the line formed west of Herr's Tavern, but the map draws Archer and Davis 185 to 220 m east of it, with Marye's guns and the two reserve brigades west of it.
v9 check: Reardon and Vossler (S55): The booklet puts the halt on Herr's Ridge two miles west of Gettysburg (p. 19), which fits the map and Davis and not Heth's "within a mile".

question: Where was Gamble's main line?
what the sources say: S02 Gamble: "about 1 mile in front of the seminary" | S09 tablet and S15 memorial stand on McPherson Ridge, well under a mile from the seminary
how the pilot handled it: Placed the line on McPherson Ridge (P04).
comment: A mile from the seminary would be at or beyond Willoughby Run. Gamble may describe his skirmish line, or estimate loosely.
v2 update: what the map adds: New evidence, and the main ruling v2 needs. The map draws the four regiments ("Morning", "9 A.M.") on the eastern arm of McPherson Ridge, about 540 m (0.34 mile) from the seminary, with Calef's guns on the pike about 300 m farther forward (872 m, 0.54 mile). Neither is a mile. Two readings: (a) the bars are the main line, with the guns and skirmishers pushed forward; (b) the bars are the line after the 200-yard fall-back, and the first line was at the guns. v2 uses the map line for P04 and leaves P05 without coordinates.
v9 check: Reardon and Vossler (S55): The booklet says only that Buford's last line was on McPherson's Ridge, a mile nearer the town than Herr's Ridge (p. 19). It supports the ridge, not a line a mile in front of the seminary, but it does not settle which arm of the ridge.

question: Who fired the first cannon shot?
what the sources say: S13 tablet: Marye's battery claims it, from the ridge west of Herr's Tavern | S15 memorial: the "opening gun" was fired from the McPherson Ridge crest by Calef's battery
how the pilot handled it: No ruling needed for positions; both batteries are placed.
comment: The marker database page notes the Confederate claim is disputed.
v2 update: what the map adds: The map prints both claims: "Opening Guns of the Battle" beside Marye's battery and "Opening Gun of the Battle" beside Calef's. It does not help decide.

question: Which sergeant had which section of Calef's battery?
what the sources say: S08 tablet: centre section under Sgt. Pergel, with the 1st Brigade | S17 (modern forum): left section under Pergel, centre under Newman, right under Roder
how the pilot handled it: Named sections by commander, not by left/centre/right (P10 to P12).
comment: Calef's own report (pt. 1, about pp. 1029-1032) should settle it; I could not retrieve it.
v2 update: what the map adds: The map labels one gun symbol south of the woods "A. 2' U.S. Calef" without naming a section (see P12).

question: How long did the cavalry hold?
what the sources say: S01 Buford: "for more than two hours" | S02 Gamble: "several hours" | S10 tablet (Devin): over two hours
how the pilot handled it: Ended the cavalry positions at 10:15 to 10:40 (P04 to P06).
v9 check: Reardon and Vossler (S55): The booklet has the cavalry's fight last from 0700 to about 1015 (p. 20), over three hours counting the delaying action back from Marsh Creek.

question: Was Reynolds killed by a shell from Pegram?
what the sources say: S04 Heth: "One of the first shells fired by Pegram mortally wounded Major-General Reynolds"
comment: Outside the pilot window. As far as I know, Reynolds is generally held to have been shot by a rifle bullet later in the morning; check before using Heth here.
v9 check: Reardon and Vossler (S55): The booklet has Reynolds killed instantly by a bullet to the back of the head as he sent the Iron Brigade into the Herbst woodlot (p. 22). That is against Heth's shell. This one could be closed.

question: When did Early's division attack?
what the sources say: S18 (the map): Gordon's line at the knoll is labelled "3 P.M." and Hays's and Hoke's lines near the town "3.45 P.M." | S16: Gordon hits the Union right at 3:30 p.m. and the Eleventh Corps withdraws at 4:00.
how the pilot handled it: Used the map: 3:00 for Gordon (row P105), 3:45 for Hays and Avery.
comment: The reports of Early and Gordon have not been read.
v9 check: Reardon and Vossler (S55): The booklet gives no clock time for Early's attack. It has Lee reach the field about 1400 and order a general assault around 1600 after hearing of Early's success (p. 26), so the attack was under way before 1600. That fits both the map's 3 P.M. and the timeline's 3:30.

question: When did Heth's second attack go in?
what the sources say: S49: "about 2:30 P.M." | S16: Pettigrew attacks at 3:00 p.m. | S18 (the map): Meredith's line is labelled "10.15 A.M. - 3 P.M.", Biddle changes position at "2.30 P.M.", Stone holds until "3.30 P.M.".
how the pilot handled it: Held as a range, 2:30 to 3:00, on rows P82 and P84; the playback shows the Confederate line on the ridge from 3:00.
comment: Heth's and Pettigrew's brigade reports for the afternoon have not been read.
v9 check: Reardon and Vossler (S55): The booklet has the third phase of the day begin around 1400, with Heth sending his two fresh brigades against the Iron Brigade (p. 23). Three sources now give 2:00, 2:30 and 3:00. The event's range was widened to 2:00 to 3:00.

question: When was Reynolds killed?
what the sources say: S16: 10:50 a.m. | The map labels the Iron Brigade's line, which he was placing, from "10.15 A.M.". Other accounts, not read here, give times from about 10:15 to 10:45.
how the pilot handled it: The event holds a range, 10:15 to 10:50, and is shown at 10:25, before the railroad cut (17 Nov 2026).
v9 check: Reardon and Vossler (S55): The booklet gives no clock time but fixes the order: Reynolds was killed moments after the Iron Brigade came up, before it drove Archer back and before the charge on the railroad cut (pp. 21-22). The First Corps arrived at roughly 1015. The event was moved from 10:50 to a range of 10:15 to 10:50, shown at 10:25, ahead of the railroad cut.

question: When was the fight at the railroad cut?
what the sources say: S18 (the map): the charge of the 95th New York, 14th Brooklyn and 6th Wisconsin is labelled "10.30 A.M." | S55: the second phase of the day ran from about 1030 to 1200, the charge came after Reynolds's death, and the fight at the cut ended about 1200 (pp. 21-23) | S16: the morning attack is over by 11:30.
how the pilot handled it: Rows P38 and P47 keep the map's 10:30. The event now holds a range, 10:30 to 12:00.
comment: The reports of Dawes (6th Wisconsin) and Davis would narrow it.
